scenarios.name: Auth cache returns stale signing keys
scenarios.title: [AUTH-01] Token validation failures after key rotation
scenarios.description: Valid tokens fail validation after a signing-key rotation. auth-service cache lookup may be returning stale key material from auth-cache.

events.description: Auth service revision deployed with key-cache behavior change
Token validation failures increase for valid users
Cache hit rate remains high while key version is stale

scenarios.root_cause: The auth-service is using stale signing-key material from auth-cache after key rotation; confirm with key-version/cache evidence before treating this as proven.
scenarios.resolution: Refresh the signing-key cache and validate key version propagation. Verify valid tokens succeed, invalid tokens remain rejected, and authentication error rate returns to baseline. Add a key-rotation integration test and cache-age alert.
scenarios.graph_hypothesis: auth-cache may contribute to auth-service token-validation failures; the configured dependency alone is not proof.

scenarios.name: Payment database connection exhaustion
scenarios.title: [PAY-01] Payment requests fail while database pool is saturated
scenarios.description: payment-api returns 500/timeouts. payment-db connection utilization is at its limit and payment-cache remains responsive.

events.description: Active database connections reach configured pool limit
Payment cache remains healthy during database saturation

scenarios.root_cause: payment-api database operations are exhausting the payment-db connection pool; validate with pool metrics and slow-query evidence.
scenarios.resolution: Identify and remediate slow or leaked database connections, then verify pool utilization falls below the alert threshold, payment requests succeed, and 5xx/latency return to baseline. Add pool saturation alerting and a peak-load regression test.
scenarios.graph_hypothesis: payment-db is a candidate contributor to payment-api errors; verify with connection and query evidence.

scenarios.name: Order flow fails on auth dependency
scenarios.title: [ORDER-01] Order submission fails during auth degradation
scenarios.description: order-service cannot complete order submission when auth-service token validation starts failing. A configured auth token validation edge connects the services.
scenarios.root_cause: Order submission is affected by authentication failures in auth-service; investigate auth-service and auth-cache evidence before confirming the initiating fault.
scenarios.resolution: Restore correct token validation in auth-service, validate the auth-cache key version, then run an end-to-end order submission and verify order success rate recovers. Add an order-to-auth integration test and downstream-impact alert.
scenarios.graph_hypothesis: auth-service degradation may propagate to order-service along the configured dependency.

scenarios.name: Notification worker backlog
scenarios.title: [NOTIFY-01] Notification delivery backlog grows
scenarios.description: notification-service delivery lag increases. Inspect Pub/Sub event delivery and downstream dependency health before attributing cause.

events.description: Order event production rate remains elevated
Notification state writes show increased latency

scenarios.root_cause: Notification delivery is delayed; candidate causes include consumer capacity, event delivery, or slow notification-state writes. Evidence is needed to distinguish them.
scenarios.resolution: Inspect consumer lag, retry/dead-letter counts, and Firestore write latency. Restore consumer capacity or remediate the verified bottleneck, then confirm queue age drains and a test notification is delivered. Add queue-age and retry alerts.
scenarios.graph_hypothesis: The graph should show configured relationships but must not infer a causal edge without supporting evidence.

scenarios.name: Payment cache stale response
scenarios.title: [PAY-02] Payment API returns stale pricing state
scenarios.description: payment-api responses appear inconsistent with the latest order state. payment-cache is a candidate source of stale values; payment-db is the source to compare against.

events.description: Cache entries exceed expected freshness window
Persisted order state differs from cached state

scenarios.root_cause: payment-api may be serving stale cached state from payment-cache; confirm against persisted payment-db state and cache freshness evidence.
scenarios.resolution: Invalidate or refresh the affected cache entries, compare API responses with persisted payment-db records, and verify repeated reads return consistent values. Add cache-age metrics and a stale-read regression test.
scenarios.graph_hypothesis: payment-cache is a candidate contributor; configured cache lookup alone does not prove the failure source.

scenarios.name: Ambiguous concurrent signals
scenarios.title: [GRAPH-01] Multiple dependency signals without proven causation
scenarios.description: auth-service and notification-service emit errors within the same window, while firestore latency is elevated. The scenario intentionally lacks direct evidence linking these signals.
scenarios.root_cause: Insufficient evidence to determine a single root cause. The signals may be correlated or independent.
scenarios.resolution: Do not apply a broad remediation based on timing alone. Collect request traces, cache key-version evidence, Firestore latency breakdowns, and event-delivery metrics. Resolve the verified fault and rerun service-specific health checks.
scenarios.graph_hypothesis: Acceptance case: graph must distinguish configured dependency edges from evidence-supported or inferred edges.
